text.p: CompUSA Inc. said Wednesday its profits jumped 27 percent in the last quarter of 1996 to a record $23.7 million despite a sharp slowdown in retail computer sales over the Christmas period.

The Dallas-based retailer of personal computers and other products said net income in its fiscal 1997 second quarter, which ended Dec. 28, climbed to $23.7 million, or 25 cents a share, from $18.7 million, or 20 cents a share, a year ago.
Total sales increased 22 percent to $1.2 billion from $983 million, although sales at the 95 stores open at least one year grew by only 1.5 percent.
"CompUSA achieved record earnings despite the highly promotional environment during the holidays and slowdown in retail sales toward the end of the season," Chief Executive Officer James Halpin said.

He told reporters CompUSA's modest same-store sales growth was "a bright spot on the PC retailing horizon" and said the company expected to increase its market share as some of its troubled rivals begin closing stores.

Tandy Corp. last month said it was selling all 17 of its Incredible Universe superstores and closing 19 of its Computer City stores. Halpin said other competitors were scaling back their range of computer products because of sluggish sales.

"We believe these changes could result in as much as $2 billion in orphaned or abandoned sales. CompUSA plans to take advantage of this unique opportunity to increase our share of the total PC market," Halpin said.

He said 1997 retail sales were "off to a good start" in January, fuelled by strong demand for Intel Corp.'s new multimedia MMX chip and for Microsoft's new Office 97 software, both of which were introduced this month.
CompUSA's earnings were in line with Wall Street's lowered expectations, and its shares rose 25 cents to $17.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

CompUSA now operates 122 "superstores" in 55 major metropolitan markets throughout the United States. Fourteen of those stores were opened in the last three months of 1996 and about 10 more are expected to open during the next six months.
The company also owns PCs Compleat Inc., a leading direct reseller of personal computers and peripherals.

About 60 percent of CompUSA's revenues come from its retail operations with the remainder coming from mail order, training and technical services, and direct sales to corporations, government and educational bodies.
The company said net income for the first six months of fiscal year 1997 rose to $38.3 million, or 40 cents a share, from $25 million, or 28 cents a share.
Sales for the six months rose by 24 percent to a record $2.19 billion from $1.77 billion, with sales at the 95 stores open one year or more expanding by 4.1 percent.
